title: How do we find the square root of 81 by taking away odd numbers?
description: The video finds the square root of eighty one by taking away odd numbers from one onwards until nothing is left, then counting them. Keeko doubts the root after naming the last odd number taken away instead of counting them.
teaching_notes: One idea: take away odd numbers from one onwards until the leftover is exactly zero, and the count of odd numbers taken away is the square root. Watch for students who give the last odd number instead of the count.

source: Find √81 by successive subtraction of odd numbers.
video_script.why: The child learns that taking away odd numbers one after another from a perfect square ends at zero, and that the number of odd numbers taken away is its square root.
video_script.substitution: Take away 1, 3, 5 and so on until the leftover is zero, then count how many odd numbers were taken away.
video_script.anchor: the number eighty one with the odd numbers one, three, five and so on lined up beside it
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko names the last odd number taken away, 17, as the square root. 17 is only the last odd number; the root is how many odd numbers were taken away, which is 9.
video_script.payoff_line: The square root of eighty one is nine

final_answer.spoken: the square root of eighty one is nine

maths_rules: the odd numbers taken away are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17: 9 of them, so √81 = 9
the slip: 17 is the last odd number taken away, not the count
video_script.design: One idea: subtract odd numbers until zero, then count. Wrong idea: naming the last odd number. The number stays in the anchor band and the leftovers drop down the working board.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='term'/>A square root of a number means a number that gives it when multiplied by itself.
<bookmark mark='num'/>Take away odd numbers from eighty one, starting from one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the square root of eighty one?

beats.on_screen: the question holds still and the empty box glows

marks.stop: the empty box glows in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Think and tell.

marks.take: the odd numbers 1, 3, 5 are taken from 9 one at a time
marks.three: the three odd numbers are counted and 3 × 3 = 9 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Try nine first. Take away one, three and five in turn.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>The leftover lands exactly on zero after three odd numbers.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Three times three is nine, so three odd numbers matched the number three.

marks.given: the number and the odd numbers are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the number is eighty one, and we subtract odd numbers from one onwards.

beats.on_screen: To find: the square root of 81

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the square root of eighty one.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, take away one, three and five. Eighty one minus one is eighty.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Eighty minus three is seventy seven, and the leftover keeps getting smaller.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Seventy seven minus five is seventy two, and the next odd number is seven.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Step two, take away seven, nine and eleven. Seventy two minus seven is sixty five.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>Sixty five minus nine is fifty six, and the odd numbers are still going up.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Fifty six minus eleven is forty five, and the next odd number is thirteen.

marks.zero: 17 − 17 = 0 is written and the 0 is ringed

narration: <bookmark mark='thirteen'/>Step three, take away thirteen, fifteen and seventeen. Forty five minus thirteen is thirty two.
<bookmark mark='fifteen'/>Thirty two minus fifteen is seventeen, and seventeen is the next odd number.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Seventeen minus seventeen is exactly zero, so we stop.

beats.on_screen: odd numbers taken away: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17: nine numbers; check: 9 × 9 = 81

marks.count: the odd numbers taken away are counted one by one, from one to nine

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step four, count the odd numbers we took away. They are one, three, five, seven, nine, eleven, thirteen, fifteen and seventeen, which is nine numbers.
<bookmark mark='check'/>To check, nine times nine is eighty one, which is the number we started with.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The square root of eighty one is nine.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: the last number taken away was 17, so the root is 17; the nine odd numbers are counted and 9 replaces it

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows the root as 17
marks.count: the nine odd numbers are counted under the bubble
marks.fix: 17 is struck and 9 takes its place

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the square root is seventeen, because seventeen was the last number taken away.
<bookmark mark='count'/>But seventeen is only the last odd number. The root is how many odd numbers were taken away.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>There were nine of them, so the root is nine.
